newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels kill four policemen in Algiers, paper.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels kill four policemen in Algiers, paper.

text.p: Moslem rebels shot and killed four policemen in three hit-and-run attacks in the Algerian capital this week, an Algerian newspaper said on Saturday.
Guerrillas shot dead two policemen while on a patrol in Bouzreah district at the northern edge of Algiers on Wednesday, El Watan newspaper said.

Another policeman was gunned down at May First square in central Algiers while he was visiting his family on Tuesday. A fourth policeman was killed on the same day in Bab el Oued -- a Moslem fundamentalist stronghold in downtown Algiers, El Watan said.

The attacks underlined the ability of the rebels to strike in the crowded streets of Algiers -- home to more than three million people -- despite a government crackdown on their cells earlier this year.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
Algeria, which has been without an elected parliament since 1992, is preparing to hold a one-stage parliamentary elections in June.
